_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 3 Mathematics unit lecture film, Lesson 2 Adding, Taking Away and Money. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow the lesson page's own steps in order - Make 100 and make 1000, Add in any order, Adding with regrouping (with its own Estimate first check), Taking away with regrouping, Money and the dot, Giving change - and every number is the lesson's: 62 and 38, 17 add 9 add 3, 247 add 185, 400 take away 178, sh 4.65 and sh 3.05, and sh 2.60 paid with sh 5.00. NOTE this lesson writes money as sh 2.60, shillings and cents with a dot, because 3Nm.01 is money notation with a decimal point; it is not the bare '10 sh' of the other Maths lessons.
title: Adding, Taking Away and Money
subtitle: Grade 3 Mathematics
objectives: Understand the commutative and associative properties of addition, and use these to simplify calculations.
Recognise complements of 100 and complements of multiples of 10 or 100 (up to 1000).
Estimate, add and subtract whole numbers with up to three digits (regrouping of ones or tens).
Interpret money notation for currencies that use a decimal point.
Add and subtract amounts of money to give change.

beats.say: Today you add big numbers, take them away, and pay for things.
You will make a hundred, carry a ten, and count out change.
A complement is what you still need to reach a round number.
You have 62. How many more make 100?
Count on to the next ten first. 62 to 70 is 8.
Then 70 to 100 is 30. And 8 and 30 make 38.
So 62 and 38 are complements. 62 add 38 is 100.
Adding can be done in any order you like. Look at 17 add 9 add 3.
Start with 17 and 3. They make 20, which is a round number.
Now 20 add 9 is 29. Choosing the order made the sum easy.
Taking away is not like this. 10 take away 3 is not 3 take away 10.
Add one column at a time, starting from the right.
247 add 185. The ones first: 7 and 5 make 12.
12 is too big for the ones. Write 2, and carry the ten.
The tens: 4 and 8 and the carried 1 make 13. Write 3, carry again.
The hundreds: 2 and 1 and 1 make 4. So the answer is 432.
Check it roughly: 200 add 200 is about 400. 432 is close.
Taking away goes down the same columns, from the right.
400 take away 178. In the ones, 0 is too small for 8.
Never swap the digits round. Fetch a ten from the left.
The hundreds lend one. 4 becomes 3, 0 becomes 9, and 0 becomes 10.
Now take away down the columns: 2, 2 and 2. That is 222.
An amount of money has a dot in it. Look at four point six five.
The four is whole shillings. The six and the five are cents.
There are 100 cents in a shilling, not ten. Read both figures.
So three point zero five is three shillings and five cents.
Not fifty cents. The zero is holding the ten cents column open.
Change is the gap between the price and what you paid.
It costs two shillings and sixty cents. You pay five shillings.
Count on. From two sixty up to three shillings is forty cents.
Then three shillings up to five is two more shillings.
So the change is two shillings and forty cents.
You can find a complement to 100, and add in any order.
You carry when a column is too big, and exchange when it is too small.
You read both figures after the dot, and count on to find change.
